capabilities_done: new src/pipeline.rs: guarded(device, label, stage, create) pushes ErrorFilter::OutOfMemory, Internal, Validation, runs the creation call under catch_unwind, pops all three (bounded 5 s each), returns PipelineFault {code, label, class, message}; codes shader_validation (module), pipeline_create (layout or pipeline, including the backend compiler), pipeline_panic, pipeline_scope_timeout; classes validation|internal|out_of_memory|panic|timeout|uncaptured; message = wgpu error text cut to FAULT_MESSAGE_MAX_BYTES (4096) on a char boundary
kernel.rs Kernel::new: every module/bind-group layout/pipeline layout/compute pipeline goes through guarded; the first failure stops the build; returns Result<Self, PipelineFault>

device.rs acquire_with: returns AcquireFailure {error, fault}; after the build a poll + loss latch check (DeviceLost{generation}) and an uncaptured-latch check (pipeline_create, class uncaptured), so the outcome is decided before any dispatch; from_external maps the fault to its GpuError

plan_sink.rs: Inner.pipeline_fault; GpuBackend::pipeline_fault() -> Option<PipelineFault> (set by acquire/reacquire failures and the probe, cleared by a successful reacquire); test-faults hook GpuBackend::probe_pipeline(wgsl, entry) builds one extra auto-layout pipeline on the live device (state unchanged; latch set -> Gpu(uncaptured_error))
plan_sink/shared.rs OutputPipeline::new: same guard (a host-owned device has no handler of ours, so the unscoped internal error would hit wgpu's default panic handler)
lib.rs: pub mod pipeline, re-export PipelineFault + FAULT_MESSAGE_MAX_BYTES, compile_fail snippet for probe_pipeline (V4-04), DESCRIPTOR pipeline_failure updated with test citations

notes.diagnosis_verified: wgpu-core 27.0.3 device/resource.rs:3595 maps hal::PipelineError::Linkage (wgpu-hal 27.0.4 dx12/shader_compilation.rs:266, FXC D3DCompile failure) to CreateComputePipelineError::Internal, webgpu_error_type Internal (pipeline.rs:264); wgpu 27.0.1 backend/wgpu_core.rs ErrorSinkRaw::handle_error_or_return_handler delivers to the innermost scope with the SAME filter, else the uncaptured handler, else default_error_handler (panic). The old Kernel::new pushed only ErrorFilter::Validation, so the FXC error latched the fault (acquire path) and became device_fault at the first dispatch, or panicked on a shared device (no handler). wgpu's own test helpers (wgpu-test fail/valid, trunk) use a Validation-only scope, which is why the pattern missed internal errors
